option.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor need not be strictly order-preserving: distinct positive elements a≤b can have equal quasitrace.
option.approach: Investigate whether the stronger configuration produced by a constant-increment sequence is impossible even when individual ordered elements can have equal quasitrace. Use several consecutive increments and their positive partial sums rather than just one ordered pair.

options.counterfactual: Every faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor is strictly order-preserving: if 0≤a≤b and a≠b, then τ(a)<τ(b).
options.approach: Audit the quasitracial ultrapower construction and apply strict order preservation there. The classes represented by (a_n) and (a_{n+1}) would have equal quasitrace but a nonzero positive difference.

options.counterfactual: The stronger configuration required by a witness is impossible: bounded positive partial sums force the quasitraces of their summands to tend to zero, even though individual ordered elements may have equal quasitrace.
options.approach: Reduce the problem to projections obtained from spectral cutoffs of the increments. Seek an exhaustion theorem excluding infinitely many projections of uniformly positive quasitrace whose finite sums have a common norm bound.
